certified.name: AWS GovCloud (US)
certified.useCase: AWS GovCloud (US) hosts VisualVault Cloud's infrastructure for the government-exclusive offering.
certified.justification: Provides FedRAMP-authorized infrastructure in U.S. government-only regions operated by screened U.S. persons, meeting federal customer requirements for data location and handling.
certified.mitigationMeasures: Controls are inherited from the AWS GovCloud (US) FedRAMP authorization (package F1603047866). Customer data is encrypted at rest with VisualVault-managed AWS KMS keys and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher; resources are segmented into VPCs with security groups permitting only required traffic.
certified.compensatingControls: Least-privilege IAM roles with multi-factor authentication for administrators; AWS CloudTrail and GuardDuty monitoring forwarded to the SIEM; AWS Config recording with a daily automated asset inventory; and encrypted backups replicated across GovCloud regions.

certified.name: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure Government)
certified.useCase: Microsoft Entra ID (via Azure Government) provides internal corporate single sign-on for personnel accessing VisualVault Cloud.
certified.justification: Centralizes identity for VisualVault personnel so administrative access to VisualVault Cloud is granted, reviewed and revoked in one place with enforced multi-factor authentication.
certified.mitigationMeasures: Controls are inherited from the Microsoft Azure Government FedRAMP authorization (package F1603087869). Entra ID authenticates VisualVault personnel only; it does not store or process federal customer data.
certified.compensatingControls: Multi-factor authentication required for all administrative sign-ins; conditional access limits administrative sign-in; access is reviewed periodically and removed promptly at offboarding; sign-in logs are retained for investigation.

certified.name: CrowdStrike Falcon Platform for Government
certified.useCase: CrowdStrike Falcon Platform for Government provides endpoint detection and response across VisualVault's corporate AWS and AWS GovCloud infrastructure, via separate subscriptions for each environment.
certified.justification: Provides continuous endpoint detection and response across VisualVault Cloud hosts, supporting rapid detection and containment of malicious activity.
certified.mitigationMeasures: Controls are inherited from the CrowdStrike Falcon Platform for Government FedRAMP authorization (package FR1807853629A). Sensors send security telemetry (process, file and network metadata), not federal customer content, over TLS; the government-environment subscription is kept separate from the corporate one.
certified.compensatingControls: Access to the Falcon console is restricted to the security team with multi-factor authentication; detections are triaged under the Incident Response Process; sensor coverage is verified against the automated asset inventory.

certified.name: KnowBe4 Platform
certified.useCase: KnowBe4 Platform provides security awareness training for VisualVault personnel.
certified.justification: Delivers and records required security awareness and role-based training for VisualVault personnel with access to the system.
certified.mitigationMeasures: Controls are inherited from the KnowBe4 FedRAMP authorization (package FR2201340492). The platform holds personnel training records only, never federal customer data, and has no connection to VisualVault Cloud systems.
certified.compensatingControls: Administrative access to KnowBe4 is limited to training administrators; completion is validated automatically by the training validators reported in the Security Decision Record; records are retained per policy.

source.evidenceName: Generating Inventories - AWS GovCloud Asset Inventory

informationResourceInventory.derivation: This list is generated automatically, not maintained by hand. aws_govcloud_asset_inventory.py 2.0.0 runs on a schedule with read-only AWS API calls across us-gov-east-1, us-gov-west-1 (and global services such as IAM, S3 and Route 53) and records every resource found in a machine-readable inventory, stored with its SHA-256 integrity hash as evidence "Generating Inventories - AWS GovCloud Asset Inventory" (EVD-AWS-GOVCLOUD-INVENTORY) in VisualVault's FedRAMP evidence repository. Each refresh of this Certification Package Overview reads the newest inventory and summarizes it by AWS service and resource type. No inventoried resource carries a FedRAMPBoundary tag, so every resource in the inventoried AWS account is treated as part of the cloud service offering (979 resources). Resource names, network addresses and identifiers are deliberately not reproduced here; the complete inventory and the code that produces it are available to assessors.

cryptographicModules.name: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) HSM
cryptographicModules.usedBy: Document Management (document encryption at rest), and the AWS services encrypted with KMS keys: Amazon S3, Amazon FSx, Amazon RDS, Amazon EBS volumes and AWS Backup
cryptographicModules.purpose: Generates, stores and protects the keys that encrypt and decrypt customer documents; key material never leaves the validated HSMs, and the application calls KMS through the AWS GovCloud FIPS endpoints.

cryptographicModules.name: AWS-LC Cryptographic Module (Elastic Load Balancing TLS termination)
cryptographicModules.usedBy: All customer-facing services: user web access, REST API integrations, anonymous forms, and Single Sign On sign-in through the Application Load Balancers
cryptographicModules.purpose: Terminates TLS 1.2/1.3 for all inbound HTTPS connections to VisualVault Cloud using FIPS-enabled ELB security policies, protecting federal customer data in transit between users or integrations and the load balancer.

independentAssessment.overallSummaryOfAssessment:
## Scope
A-LIGN performed an independent FedRAMP 20x Class B assessment of VisualVault Cloud against the FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026. The assessment covered all Key Security Indicators and FedRAMP rules applicable to a 20x Class B certification, including the cloud service offering, the third-party information resources it relies on, and the personnel and processes that operate it.

## Approach
A-LIGN verified and validated each KSI and rule through examination of provider-supplied evidence and, where applicable, testing of technical telemetry and configuration data. Evidence was delivered through the provider's continuous evidence pipeline in Paramify, allowing A-LIGN to assess the current operating state of the cloud service offering rather than point-in-time documentation alone. Each KSI and rule was evaluated against the current rule text and its Class B applicability. All evidence was reviewed by the lead assessor and an independent second reviewer. Results for each KSI and rule are recorded in the Security Decision Record.

## Results
Based on the procedures performed, A-LIGN determined that VisualVault Cloud satisfies the KSIs and FedRAMP rules applicable to a 20x Class B certification. Issues identified during the assessment were remediated by the provider and re-validated by A-LIGN prior to completion. No failures remain open.

## Areas of Dispute
There are no areas of dispute between A-LIGN and VisualVault.

relevantPolicies.name: Physical and Environmental Protection Policy (POLICY-0010)
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for physical and environmental protection of information systems, based on NIST SP 800-53 (Moderate) controls. It covers infrastructure hosting requirements (FedRAMP-authorized IaaS), alternate work site/remote access rules such as VPN and encryption requirements, and controls over the delivery and removal of equipment from VisualVault facilities.

relevantPolicies.name: Security Assessment and Authorization Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy defines requirements for security assessment and authorization of information systems, based on NIST SP 800-53 (Moderate) controls. It covers independent and internal security assessments, system interconnections, plans of actions and milestones, security authorization, and continuous monitoring, including coordination with FedRAMP JAB/AO and third-party assessors.

relevantPolicies.name: SOP-0030 - Information Release
relevantPolicies.summary: This procedure establishes controls to prevent unintended disclosure or spillage of information when VisualVault posts content to publicly accessible systems. It defines authorized personnel and locations for public postings, a review/approval workflow, and additional safeguards (redaction, NDAs, encryption) for releasing sensitive or confidential information such as during sales cycles.

relevantPolicies.name: VisualVault Audit and Accountability Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy (Policy-0013) establishes VisualVault's requirements for auditing and accountability across its information systems, based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) and NIST SP 800-92 guidelines. It defines requirements for audit scope, event logging, time synchronization, log review/monitoring, protection and retention of audit records, and roles responsible for enforcement and oversight.

relevantPolicies.name: Contingency Planning Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes requirements for contingency planning based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls, covering disaster recovery/business continuity plan development, distribution, training, and testing. It also details information system backup requirements, data retention schedules, and data restoration testing procedures.

relevantPolicies.name: POLICY-0019 – Personnel Management Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's personnel management program, based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls, covering all personnel and third parties using VisualVault systems. It defines a four-level corrective action/sanctions framework for security and confidentiality violations, along with notification, enforcement, and review responsibilities.

relevantPolicies.name: Media Protection Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for handling digital and non-digital media, based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls. It covers media access authorization, marking, storage, transport, and sanitization, along with roles, responsibilities, exceptions, and enforcement procedures.

relevantPolicies.name: Access, Identification, and Authentication Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes access control, identification, and authentication requirements based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (Moderate) baseline controls. It covers topics such as least privilege, user registration, role-based access control, session/account protections, separation of duties, network access control, external systems, device identification, and multi-factor authentication.

relevantPolicies.name: Personnel Security Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for personnel security based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (Moderate) controls, covering position risk designation, personnel screening and rescreening, hiring, training, termination, transfers, and third-party personnel requirements. It defines responsibilities for management, the Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance, employees, and third parties to ensure physical and system access is properly authorized and monitored throughout the employment lifecycle.

relevantPolicies.name: Vendor Management Policy
relevantPolicies.fileName: (SR-01) Supply Chain and Vendor Risk Management Policy.pdf
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for managing third-party IT vendors and partners to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of its systems and data. It covers vendor inventory and risk classification, contract security requirements (including for cloud service providers and telecommunications vendors), and change management processes for vendor-provided services.

relevantPolicies.name: Information Security Policy (POLICY-0009)
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes the organization's information security program based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls, covering security awareness/training (SETA), incident response and handling, information spillage response, and security planning (system security plan and security architecture). It defines roles and responsibilities (e.g., CTO, Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance) and enforcement procedures for all VisualVault personnel, third parties, and information systems.

relevantPolicies.name: Mobile Device Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes security requirements and user responsibilities for mobile device usage, including laptops, portable devices (tablets/smartphones), and BYOD/POCD devices connecting to corporate systems. It also covers 802.11 Wi-Fi security controls and is based on NIST SP 800-124 guidance, fulfilling NIST 800-53 control AC-19.

relevantPolicies.name: Risk Assessment Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes requirements for risk assessment and vulnerability management based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls. It covers security categorization, periodic risk assessments, vulnerability scanning (external, internal, and change-triggered), scanning tool requirements, vulnerability review, remediation timelines by severity, and reporting to leadership and FedRAMP officials. It also defines roles and responsibilities, primarily for VisualVault Management and the Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance.

relevantPolicies.name: Operations Management Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes IT operations security requirements based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls, covering system maintenance, boundary and transmission protection, cryptographic key management, and system/information integrity practices such as flaw remediation, malicious code protection, and monitoring. It also defines roles and responsibilities for management, the Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance, personnel, and third parties, along with enforcement procedures for policy violations.

relevantPolicies.name: Configuration Management Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy defines requirements for configuration management of information systems based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (Moderate) controls. It covers baseline configurations, change control, access restrictions, configuration settings, least functionality, system component inventory, configuration management planning, and software usage/installation restrictions. It also outlines roles, responsibilities, enforcement, and revision history.

relevantPolicies.name: Systems and Services Acquisition Policy (POLICY-0012)
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for acquiring, developing, and testing information systems, components, and services, based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (Moderate) controls. It covers the system development lifecycle, acquisition process criteria, documentation requirements, external information system services (including FedRAMP, CJIS, and HIPAA considerations), and developer configuration management and security testing obligations. Roles and responsibilities for VisualVault management, the Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance, personnel, and third parties are also defined.
